# tools-ssh

SSH: shell commands on another host, through TRAMP.

- **Runs in:** the harness process
- **Source:** [lisp/modules/harness-tools-ssh.el](../../lisp/modules/harness-tools-ssh.el)
- **Loaded:** when enabled (see `harness-enable-modules`)
- **Requires:** [tools](tools.md), [tools-shell](tools-shell.md)

## About

The ssh tool runs a shell command on another machine.  It goes
through TRAMP, as everything the harness does on a remote host does:
the command runs with `harness-run-command` in a TRAMP directory,
/ssh:HOST:/DIR/, so it shares TRAMP's connection to HOST and its
settings (`tramp-remote-path`, proxies, connection sharing).  The
other tools reach the same host the same way: the file tools take
TRAMP paths (read_file /ssh:HOST:/etc/hosts; write_file, edit_file,
list_dir, glob, grep and file_info alike) and bash runs on HOST given
a cwd there.  The tool's description says so, and its result names
the directory it ran in as such a path.

HOST is what ssh takes -- an alias of ~/.ssh/config or
[USER@]HOST[:PORT] -- an ssh:// URL, or a TRAMP prefix:
/ssh:USER@HOST#PORT:, or /ssh:JUMP|ssh:HOST: through a jump host.
It is checked before TRAMP sees it (`harness-tools-ssh-prefix`):
TRAMP hands host, user and port to a local shell and to ssh, which
takes a word starting with a dash for an option (-oProxyCommand=...),
so only the characters of host names, user names and ports get
through, and only the methods of `harness-tools-ssh--methods`, which
all log in with ssh: /sudo::/ and /docker:...: are no hosts.

Permissions: a call is of kind exec, so the permission mode and the
auto-mode judge decide it as they decide a bash command, and its path
is the directory it runs in on HOST, so the jail asks for HOST the
first time.  The path is worked out without connecting -- nothing in
the permission chain may wait on the network -- and only HOST knows
where its login's home directory is.  So a call that runs there (no
cwd, a cwd starting with ~, a relative cwd) is about the home
directory as TRAMP writes it, /ssh:HOST:~/ or /ssh:HOST:~/src/, a
place of its own that the chain never expands (`harness-remote-home-p`),
and the first prompt for a host asks for that, not for the whole
host.  A cwd that leaves the home (~/..) or is another user's (~bob)
is about the host's root, /ssh:HOST:/, which the prompt offers as its
widest answer; an absolute cwd is about itself.  Granting /ssh:HOST:/
lets a session work anywhere on HOST, home directory included, with
this tool and every other; granting /ssh:HOST:~/ only the home
directory, and /ssh:HOST:/home/u/ not that, since the harness does not
know where the home is.  A non-interactive session needs the grant
beforehand (`harness-allowed-directories`).  The prompt for the
call itself offers lasting answers for this host alone
(`harness-perms--cover-ladder`).  Corporate mode turns the tool off
(see harness-tools.el).

The harness has no terminal: a connection that needs a password, a
key passphrase or a host key confirmation fails.  Then ssh is asked
once more, in batch mode, why, and the error carries its answer and
how to set the host up (`harness-tools-remote-failure`, which
explains the other tools' failed connections too).  The command runs
with bash, or sh on a host without bash, its standard input
/dev/null (see `harness-tools-shell-remote-command`).

## Provides

### Tools

- `ssh` — Run a shell command on another host over ssh, through TRAMP. host is an alias from ~/.ssh/config, [user@]host[:port], or a TRAMP prefix such as /ssh:user@host#2222: (/ssh:jump|ssh:host: through a jump host). The command runs with bash (sh where the host has none) in cwd, by default the remote home directory, with no input. Output is what it printed, stderr mixed in, then the exit status and the directory it ran in, as a TRAMP path. The other tools work on the host too: give read_file, write_file, edit_file, list_dir, glob, grep and file_info a path there, such as /ssh:host:/etc/hosts, and bash a cwd there; prefer them to cat, sed or grep over ssh. Nothing can answer a prompt: the host must accept a key from ssh-agent (or one without a passphrase) and be in known_hosts.
